 S Badrinath backs Hardik Pandya to Punjab Kings, suggests Mumbai Indians release Deepak Chahar
 Former Chennai Super Kings batter S Badrinath has endorsed Mumbai Indians' retention strategy for IPL 2027, backing trades involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh.
 By CricTracker Staff Published - 16 Nov 2026, 16:46 IST 
 3 Min Read
 S Badrinath backs Hardik Pandya to Punjab Kings, suggests Mumbai Indians release Deepak Chahar (Photo by Pankaj Nangia/Getty Images) Former Chennai Super Kings batter S Badrinath has shared his thoughts on Mumbai Indians' retention and release strategy ahead of the IPL 2027 auction. The five-time champions endured a disappointing campaign in 2026, finishing ninth in the standings with just four victories from 14 matches. With the franchises set to submit their retention lists by November 17, Badrinath has identified players he believes Mumbai should retain and those they could part ways with.
 One of his major recommendations was to release India pacer Deepak Chahar, who joined Mumbai Indians for ₹9.25 crore but struggled to deliver consistent performances. Chahar featured in only eight matches during the previous season, picking up eight wickets at an average of 33.12 and an economy rate of 10.39. His injury concerns and relatively expensive performances have raised questions about his place in the squad.
 S Badrinath backs Shardul Thakur, Trent Boult and other MI players 
 While Badrinath favoured releasing Chahar, he backed several other players to remain part of Mumbai Indians' plans for the next season. The former CSK batter supported retaining Shardul Thakur, who finished as the franchise's joint second-highest wicket-taker in IPL 2026 with 12 wickets.
 Badrinath also included New Zealand pacer Trent Boult in his retention picks despite his underwhelming campaign. Boult played five matches and managed only two wickets last season. The former cricketer also backed Afghanistan spinner Allah Ghazanfar and West Indies all-rounder Sherfane Rutherford as players Mumbai should continue to invest in.
 S Badrinath backs Hardik Pandya-Arshdeep Singh trade between MI and PBKS 
 Badrinath also expressed his approval of the trade involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh between Punjab Kings and Mumbai Indians. Under the deal, Hardik moved to Punjab Kings for a revised fee of ₹18 crore, while Arshdeep joined Mumbai Indians for the same amount.

 "Hardik Pandya is the biggest all-rounder in the world for Punjab Kings. The only thing is that he will play under Shreyas as captain. We all know that he won't be captain. But it is a superb signing. He is an all-rounder with experience and a good hitter down the order."
 Meanwhile, Badrinath believes Arshdeep's arrival will strengthen Mumbai's pace attack, particularly because of his ability to bowl at the death. The left-arm pacer has established himself as an important member of India's limited-overs bowling unit.
 "Arshdeep is probably among the best death bowlers in India right now. I think it is a big positive for Mumbai Indians because he is a left-armer, bowls well, is at his peak and is playing for the Indian team. So it is a win-win for both teams," he said on his YouTube channel.
 The IPL 2027 auction is scheduled to take place on December 16, 2026, with all franchises required to submit their retention lists by November 17. Mumbai Indians will be looking to make the right squad decisions after their disappointing ninth-place finish in the previous season.
